source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001], I’ve decided to upload the book initially to IPFS through Pinata. That way, if the project flops or my story isn’t received well, I’ll still have the option to remove it.

How would we ensure that only NFT holders can access it?
My idea was to gate the PDF with Lit Protocol and have the metadata point to a gated viewer that checks ownership automatically, without a manual connection. However, I’m open to your recommendation for the smoothest UX.

Also, you still need to adjust it so the cover can be viewed in full.

If my company registration is rejected again—it has already been rejected 4 times, although it should be approved today—can we proceed with a crypto-only launch and then implement Transack in the coming days/weeks once it is approved?

value_updates.access_policy: Only NFT holders may access the ebook PDF

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Yes — you’ve got it.
Datil is Lit Protocol’s current mainnet, while Serrano is now testnet / legacy.

Fortunately, this makes no conceptual difference to our approach.

Here’s what needs to happen:

- Run production gating on Datil
- If necessary, use Serrano only for local/testing (optional)
- Set up Lit access control to verify Base ERC-721 ownership
- Encrypt the PDF once, then gate access through Lit nodes


The user experience remains unchanged — they open the reader, and it automatically verifies NFT ownership.

I’ll take care of:

- The correct network configuration (Datil)
- Encryption and access rules
- Integrating the viewer

There’s nothing you need to configure on your side other than approving this approach.

value_updates.ownership_verification_rule: Verify Base ERC-721 ownership before decrypting the ebook
value_updates.content_protection: Encrypt the PDF once and gate decryption through Lit nodes
value_updates.reader_access_ux: Automatically verify NFT ownership when the reader opens
